proof_explanation: The proof is reflexive. Since negate(value) is defined to return Bool.not(value) by its function definition, the equality negate(value) == Bool.not(value) holds definitionally for all Bool values. The reflexivity tactic {==} establishes this identity.

seeded_attack.reason: The buggy implementation violates the law because negate(value) returns the input value unchanged instead of applying Boolean negation. When value is True, it returns True instead of False; when value is False, it returns False instead of True. This fails to satisfy the law requirement that negate(value) == Bool.not(value) for all Bool values.
